sentences.text: Residents like Sam told the BBC they were shocked by their blood test results Blood tests have found "really high levels" of a cancer-causing forever chemical in dozens of people living near a major chemical factory in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: The residents, from Thornton-Cleveleys, Lancashire, have been told they could be at elevated risk of serious health conditions from the substance, known as PFOA.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: The village has been under investigation for years by the Environment Agency over contamination of soils and locally grown food from the substance, which is a type of forever chemical - so-called because they do not easily break down.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: That investigation said high levels likely came from the nearby AGC Chemicals factory, which used it to manufacture coating for frying pans until 2012.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Sam and her husband, both from the village, have been told they were at increased risk of health impacts from PFOA.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: However, she told the BBC was more shocked by her son's result.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: "When we opened the results...it was like, my God, that is ridiculously off the scale.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: "I feel guilty because I've introduced [my children] to that way of life.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: I know it isn't my fault, but the guilt is horrific.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Knowing that I've offloaded what levels I probably had over the years into those children when I breastfed them - that's heartbreaking," she said.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Forever chemicals are a group of substances, also known as PFAS, that are resistant to water and oil and are in thousands of everyday products, such as clothing and cookwear.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: But because they do not break down easily they have raised health concerns.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: PFOA has been banned in the UK since 2020 because it was classed by the World Health Organisation (WHO) as a Group 1 carcinogen, which means there is clear scientific evidence it can increase the risk of cancer.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: The Environment Agency and Wyre Council have been testing the area close to the AGC Chemicals factory since 2024 to determine if it has been contaminated.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: They found PFOA at elevated levels in the soil, eggs and locally grown vegetables.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Two allotment sites have now been closed and are due to be classified as contaminated land, while residents within 1km of the factory have been advised to peel any fruit or vegetables grown in their gardens.

sentences.text: Those investigations concluded the PFOA was likely to have come from the factory having been carried in the air.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Two allotments in Thornton-Cleveleys have been closed and are due to be classified as contaminated land Residents previously asked the council to test their blood for the chemical.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: But according to the UK Health Security Agency, PFAS monitoring is not currently recommended because "tests are unlikely to provide clear information for individuals".
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Instead independent tests were offered by Manchester Metropolitan University, paid for by investigative journalists Watershed and Law for Change - which funds cases covering environmental issues.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Forty-nine residents volunteered, and they were told their blood test readings on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Andrew Molloy found out he was in the highest-risk category.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: "I was half expecting it to be just normal," he said.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: "Because the investigation here has all been focused on - you're only really being at risk if you eat fruit and veg from the garden or grow your own eggs - which I don't." Andrew's home was built on land that used to be part of the factory.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: He underwent the tests because he was worried about persistent health problems in his family.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: "One of the first things I'm going to do is take [the results] to my GP and at least get it on my record.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: They seem to refuse to do anything related to this, but now I have hard information and data," he said.
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: Mario Panteli, who was visibly shaken by his results, which were among the highest, said it was "quite emotional, a shock".
sentences.article_title: Blood tests find high level of cancer-causing forever chemical in residents near factory

sentences.text: He added: "I bought a property, assuming that this is our forever home.

sentences.text: I'm going to have to stop my children from going in the garden, front and back.

sentences.text: I feel constricted, like I'm in a cage now." Dr David Megson, who carried out the testing at Manchester Metropolitan University, said the results made him feel sick.

sentences.text: The Conservatives have promised to prevent long-term jobless benefit claimants from spending their welfare payments on alcohol, cigarettes and gambling.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Under the party's proposals, claimants who have been unemployed for more than six months would see their Universal Credit cut by 30% if they have not previously paid enough into the system, despite being able to work.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: This reduced rate would be paid onto a "Back to Work" card, which would not allow cash withdrawals or spending on these items.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Tories said the proposals were designed to encourage people back into work and cut the soaring welfare bill but Labour branded the scheme "unworkable".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: A Labour Party spokesperson said: "The Conservatives had 14 years to fix our welfare system but they completely failed to make meaningful reforms.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Under the proposals, anyone fit to work would get six months on full benefits to find a job.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Every two years a claimant has previously worked would buy an extra year on the full rate of Universal Credit - but those who have not contributed enough would drop to a new "Subsistence Allowance", worth 70% of the full rate.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The party said this would protect "those with a strong employment record".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Claimants who are sick, disabled or already in work would also be exempt, with only those judged capable of work affected.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: The Tories said loading the "Subsistence Allowance" onto a pre-paid card, with restrictions on what the money can be spent on, would ensure taxpayers' money supports claimants with essentials like food.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the current system "where someone who can work chooses not to, and earns more benefits than someone in a job" was "unfair".
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "The best welfare is a well-paid job.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: So, we will be tough on those who exploit the system because the current system is unfair to workers, taxpayers and those who truly need support," she said.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "Welfare must be a safety net for those who genuinely need it, not a lifestyle choice for those who can't be bothered." However, Helen Barnard, director of policy and research at the anti-poverty charity Trussell, said the proposals were "deeply misguided".

sentences.text: "We see people's health being damaged and their ability to find and maintain work undermined by the severe hardship so many are facing." sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Migrant boat arrives on beach near Folkestone The Home Secretary has said migrant landings on UK beaches are "not acceptable", as she ordered an urgent review after two boats reached Kent without being intercepted.

sentences.article_title: Home secretary says undetected migrant landings 'unacceptable'

sentences.text: Lauren Evans was just seven-years-old when she started getting chronic migraines Warning: This article contains details and references to suicide When Lauren Evans told her doctor she was suicidal because of the "pure agony" of her chronic migraine, she was told she was being dramatic.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: Lauren, 29, was seven when she got her first migraine and went on to have them regularly - by the time she was 24, they were happening every day.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: "People need to understand that a migraine is a full body experience," she said.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: Migraines are often misunderstood as "just a headache" despite being a neurological condition that can leave people unable to work, socialise or function in everyday life, according to a migraine expert.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it was working to improve access to neurological services.

sentences.text: "I would wake up daily either in pain or worried about when it would start." She also spent a huge amount of time researching triggers and spent "hundreds on various things just to see if that would help" - from vitamins to chiropractors.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: Lauren was training to become a biomedical scientist in the NHS but the lights and overstimulation of Singleton Hospital were so intense she had daily migraines.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: Lauren says she had her first migraine when she was a child She added that she often felt dismissed by colleagues who implied she was faking her condition but was lucky that her manager was supportive.

sentences.text: Some colleagues would accommodate her by turning off the lights, she said, but others said: "If you don't get your annual leave approved, you can just say you've got a migraine and you won't come in.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: So you're battling, not just your physical health.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: You're battling all the mental side that comes with it as well.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: There wasn't a day without pain and if there was, I'd be waiting for it." To manage her symptoms, Lauren changed her working hours, starting at 08:00 BST and finishing at 16:00 so she could get home to take medication, but was still "in agony".
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: Lauren, pictured on a trip to north Wales with her dog and boyfriend, says her new medication is working well now Experiences like Lauren's are all too common, said Katy Munro, senior GP headache specialist at the National Migraine Centre and host of the Heads Up podcast.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: "There are various barriers to people getting good help for migraine," she said.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: "What we're trying to get away from is that preconception that migraine is just a very bad headache." Munro said headaches were a symptom of migraine attacks, but so too are "visual disturbances, nausea and vomiting, sometimes numbness and tingling, sometimes abdominal pain, sometimes dizziness".
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: They are also a spectrum condition, she said, from episodic - meaning people have mild or rare attacks - to chronic where they have more than 15 days a month affected by migraine symptoms.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: "If you have a migraine attack and you put up with it and then you have another one and put up with it, your brain actually gets more irritable," she said.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: That means the migraines become more regular and can become chronic if effective treatment is not applied.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: The first barrier to treatment, Munro said, is that a lot of people believe they are "normal headaches".
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: She said people should always get repetitive headaches checked out by a GP.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: The next barrier is that GPs often just note down the headaches as a symptom rather than diagnose migraine.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: The third barrier is the medication that was offered in the past, though this has improved in the last five years, she said.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: "We need better education throughout the whole of society about how significant migraine is to people who suffer from it." The Welsh government said it recognised the effect migraines can have on people's lives and that guidance was available to help NHS staff diagnose and manage conditions.
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: The UK government said National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) had "clear guidance on the diagnosis and management of migraines, and we expect healthcare professionals to follow it and deliver high-quality care to all patients".
sentences.article_title: I couldn't live with the agony of migraines any more but my GP called me dramatic

sentences.text: After Prime Minister Andy Burnham put Russia-linked disinformation campaigns under the spotlight, BBC Verify has been examining how these attempts to influence people's opinions work.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: We have tracked – and debunked – numerous online disinformation campaigns produced by Russia-linked groups that have attempted to shift public opinion on issues like the war with Ukraine, influence elections in the US and Germany, damage social cohesion and undermine trust in authorities or institutions.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: In his UN speech, Burnham said there was an "insidious campaign" being carried out by the Russian government to target people in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: Last year, a series of fake videos featuring British public sector workers appeared online.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: Among them was a 999 call operator in Preston named Aaron, who told BBC Verify he was shocked to find out his voice had been cloned with AI to create a fake video of him talking about the 2025 Polish presidential election.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: This video can not be played British 999 call handler's voice cloned by Russian network using AI Those videos are part of a major Russian-linked disinformation campaign known as Matryoshka, which BBC Verify and other research groups have been tracking.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: AI is used to create fake videos - sometimes dozens a day - which impersonate journalists and major news organisations like the BBC to push disinformation about Ukraine and Western countries onto people's social media feeds.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: But Aaron's case indicates ordinary British citizens could also be a target.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: In the run-up to the 2024 US presidential election, BBC Verify reported how there was a shift in focus from Ukraine to post fabricated videos about the US election.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: We are once again seeing early evidence of similar misleading videos ahead of November's US midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has previously exposed a large-scale disinformation campaign run by a former US police officer now based in Russia .
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: With the help of AI, the operation created hundreds of fake local news websites in the UK, US, France and other Western countries with the aim of spreading completely made-up stories.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: A screenshot of a fake local news website produced by a Russia-linked disinformation operation One of these was a fake news website called the London Crier which falsely claimed that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had bought a mansion owned by King Charles at a bargain price.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: It was seen by hundreds of thousands of users on X and shared by an official Russian embassy account.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: We also found that a fake AI-narrated video on YouTube was the source of the bogus story.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: The platform removed it after we reported it.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: And in 2023, BBC Verify found a major propaganda operation involving bogus accounts on TikTok , which posted misleading videos in multiple languages - including English - generating millions of views, with the aim of influencing the views of users in several European countries about the war in Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: TikTok removed more than 12,000 fake accounts involved in the operation, saying its investigation indicated that the accounts originated from Russia.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: While the documents appeared to be genuine, Reddit later confirmed in a statement the leak "was part of a campaign that has been reported as originating from Russia".
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: But there are questions about how widespread or effective some of these disinformation campaigns are in reality.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: While many of them appear to be extensive and organised, it is hard to determine how widely they have spread or how significant a role they have played in actually influencing people.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: Russia is also not alone in using industrial-scale disinformation campaigns which spread false information to further its own geopolitical aims, as other authoritarian governments like China, North Korea and Iran are also major players in online disinformation.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has previously reported on a number of X accounts posting in support of Scottish independence , but whose location information indicated they originated from Iran.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: And, at the height of the Coronavirus pandemic, the BBC discovered a network of more than 1,200 faked or hijacked accounts on Facebook, Twitter and YouTube that posted pro-Chinese government and anti-US messages.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: There is evidence to suggest Western governments also engage in disinformation campaigns, although the scale of their operations are not always clear.

sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: And Meta has previously removed an influence campaign originating from France that targeted a number of countries in Africa , external .
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: AI has also exacerbated the spread of disinformation, as images can now be more easily faked and videos misleadingly edited using text prompts.
sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?

sentences.text: Text generation has also improved and can create plausible, authoritative and coherent sounding fake news reports.

sentences.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI has become a key figure in the AI technology development.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: The heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face have told the UN that the current pace of artificial intelligence (AI) development, and the risks it poses to society, demands international coordination.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Altman called for common risk evaluation standards, as did Dario Amodei of Anthropic, a main rival of OpenAI, and Clement Delangue of Hugging Face.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Amodei wrote an essay welcomed by Altman and others calling an AI development slowdown in response to fears about the technology's threat to humanity.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: However, at the same UN conference, a key technology advisor to US President Donald Trump, rejected the idea any new form of AI regulation.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Michael Kratsios, a former Uber executive, admitted that the speed of AI development is increasing and that there are risks presented by the technology, but told the UN this was not reason enough "to pause development or constrain it with new global governance structures".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: "International dialogue in this forum and others cannot be allowed to drift toward global governance," Kratsios added.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Kratsios's comments echoed similar statements made by Trump in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Trump told the UN on Tuesday he wanted to rebrand it "super intelligence" and has strongly opposed any idea of an AI slowdown because of the US's competitive advantage in the sector.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins ," he said earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI and other AI chief executives expressed a different view in their talks to the UN on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone," said Altman.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: He told the UN that he wanted countries to start working together toward "the collective good in the face of powerful new technology".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: He called for "national and international" AI standards on measuring the capabilities of an AI tool, assessing related risks, AI safeguards, and the degree to which human oversight over such tools is maintained.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: He also called for "speedy incident reporting, classification, and reporting protocols so the world can learn from failures before they become catastrophes".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: "We need common standards so countries can compare evidence, verify compliance, and have a shared language and understanding what is happening," Altman added.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Amodei said that AI "if managed poorly... could be a risk to humanity as a whole".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.article_title: OpenAI and Anthropic bosses push UN for global terms on AI

sentences.text: Catherine Walker was the legal guardian of the nine-year-old boy A woman who worked at Nottinghamshire Police has been jailed after the death of a nine-year-old boy in her care.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Catherine Walker, 47, was the legal guardian of the boy, who was found unresponsive in his bedroom in Warsop, Nottinghamshire, on 16 December 2024.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Despite the efforts of paramedics and people at the scene, the boy died in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: The force said an investigation found "clear mistreatment of the boy over a prolonged period of time".
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Walker, of Appleton Street in Warsop, was jailed for six years at Nottingham Crown Court on Monday after pleading guilty to two counts of assault/ill-treat/neglect/abandon a child/young person to cause unnecessary suffering/injury.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: The force, which has not revealed what Walker's role was, said her former husband was the boy's primary carer and had been mainly responsible for his treatment.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: He died shortly after the boy's death, police added.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Walker was sentenced at Nottingham Crown Court on Monday Officers investigating what had happened raised concerns about the conditions in the boy's bedroom, which police said "lacked any of the comforts seen elsewhere in the house".
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: There were no blinds or curtains in the window, and an electric socket was "hanging dangerously off the wall".
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: The bedroom had very little furniture, no radiator or door handle, and was fitted with a bathroom-style door lock on the outside, the force added.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Walker claimed the room was being renovated, but police said further investigation "revealed this to be untrue".
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: Officers also received evidence from other witnesses that showed "clear mistreatment of the boy over a prolonged period of time".
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: After Walker's sentencing, Det Ch Insp Gail Routledge said: "This was one of the most upsetting cases I can remember.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: "This boy was very clearly mistreated for a significant period of time and was living in conditions that no child should have to endure.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: "It was always our case that this mistreatment was a deliberate choice by the defendant, rather than the result of neglectful parenting.
sentences.article_title: Police worker jailed after death of boy in her care

sentences.text: "I am please she has now been held to account for her role in his death." Tell us which stories we should cover in Nottingham Listen to BBC Radio Nottingham on Sounds and follow BBC Nottingham on Facebook , external , on X , external , or on Instagram , external .

sentences.text: Linda and Geoff Kitchen were beginning a six-week holiday to Singapore, Indonesia and Australia when their flight experienced severe turbulence A British man who died on board a Singapore Airlines flight suffered a cardiac arrest after the plane was hit by severe turbulence, an inquest has been told.

sentences.text: Lee's father Colum and sister Colleen made four 999 calls after Lee experienced breathing problems The sister of a man who died after waiting hours for an ambulance has said his family lives every day with a "heavy heart" in the knowledge that his death was preventable.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: Lee Gannon died at the Royal Victoria Hospital in February 2022 after experiencing breathing problems at his home in Belfast.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: A post-mortem examination found he died from lobar pneumonia - a severe bacterial infection.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: The 25-year-old's family called an ambulance but the call was not deemed as a Category 1 emergency and Lee did not reach hospital for almost four hours after the initial 999 call.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: Delivering the inquest verdict, the coroner said the delay "materially contributed to his premature death".
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: Colleen said her brother was "not just a name" or a number or a recorded call by the ambulance service but a much-loved brother and son who was kind, humorous and deeply cherished.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: "I stand here today with a heavy heart, I will struggle to find the words to express the pain and devastation that our family has endured." Colleen added that after Lee's death their mother died and said she can not explain the "pain" the effects the inquest had on her.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: "Five years on we are still here and we are still grieving.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: "Lee should still be here, our mum should still be here." She said she hopes her brother's death will "bring about change".
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: At the inquest, she and her father Colum were told their family's actions, which included making four 999 calls and carrying out chest compressions, were the right thing to do.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: Lee Gannon died in February 2022 after experiencing breathing problems at his home in Belfast The coroner, Marie Dougan, said the initial 999 call made by the family should have been registered as a Category 1 - reserved for immediately life-threatening medical conditions - but it was not.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: There were two further missed opportunities to reassess and re-triage the case by ambulance operators when the family described Lee's deteriorating condition.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: After the fourth 999 call Lee was re-triaged as Category 1, but the coroner said by the time the paramedics arrived it was too late.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: "I find that the incorrect categorisation of the initial 999 call and the subsequent failures to re-triage the deceased resulted in a substantial delay in ambulance attendance and transfer to hospital," the coroner said.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: "The evidence before me demonstrated the significant effect which prolonged hospital handover delays can have upon the availability of ambulance resources to respond to patient in the community," Dougan said.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: She acknowledged that the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service (NIAS) was open throughout the inquest, had accepted fault and were committed to learning from his death.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: The court heard how Lee's mother Anne was devoted to her son and that he was known kindly as a mummy's boy who loved living in the family home.
sentences.article_title: We live with a 'heavy heart' knowing my brother's death was preventable

sentences.text: Dougan said while it was Anne's desire to understand what had happened to her son that night, it was a matter of great sadness that she hadn't survived to hear the findings.

sentences.text: National Fire Chiefs Council says half of UK fire services surveyed reported "frequently" encountering "insufficient flow" Fire hydrants in the UK often do not provide enough water flow for firefighting, fire chiefs have warned.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: A report published by the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) claims that inadequate water supplies across the UK are impacting fire crews' "ability to respond effectively" and putting the public at risk.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: It carried out a survey of UK fire services which suggested that 81% have had to change their emergency response plans due to concerns over adequate water supplies.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: "The very least firefighters should be able to rely on is access to the water they need to protect people," said NFCC chairman Phil Garrigan.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: The report calls for firefighting water supplies to be recognised as a critical public safety requirement, for "greater accountability" for the water sector and for increased hydrant maintenance.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: Fire hydrants in the UK are access points that allow crews to access mains water  when they arrive at the scene of a blaze.

sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: It provided the example of West Midlands Fire Service, which experienced water pressure issues over several days during the major wildfire in Stourbridge last month.

sentences.text: During the height of the blaze, it took 40 minutes to refill its water carrier due to reduced pressure - and crews had to rely on an additional high-volume pump for water supply.

sentences.text: The report claims firefighters had to deal with water flow issues when responding to August's Stourbridge wildfire, which saw 19 residential homes destroyed "Firefighters cannot fight fires without water," said Mr Garrigan.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: "That sounds obvious, yet our evidence shows four in five fire and rescue services have had to change response plans because of concerns about firefighting water supplies," he said.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: The organisation has called on water regulators to enforce measures on water providers regarding the provision of water for firefighting, and to implement "clear national standards" on fire hydrant repair and maintenance.

sentences.text: It also urged the UK government to ensure that fire and rescue services are recognised as "key stakeholders" within the water sector.
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: In response, Ofwat said it would consider the points raised in the NFCC's report and added that water companies do "have a duty to supply fire and rescue services to support firefighting".
sentences.article_title: Many hydrants lacking flow needed for firefighting needs, fire chiefs say

sentences.text: "We would expect water companies and fire services to work together to ensure this is the case," a spokesperson said.

sentences.text: Urfan Sharif was jailed for life for the murder of his daughter at their home in Woking Two prisoners have pleaded not guilty to the attempted murder of Urfan Sharif, who is serving a life sentence for killing his 10-year-old daughter, Sara Sharif.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, were charged last month following an attack in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, which reportedly left Sharif with cuts to his face.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Sharif and Sara's stepmother, Beinash Batool, were sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Sansom and Watson appeared at the Old Bailey via video links from HMP Wakefield on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: The hearing was told how Samsom reportedly invited Sharif into a cell at Belmarsh, where Watson was waiting, at which point Watson allegedly took hold of him and punched him repeatedly before Sansom applied pressure to his throat.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Prosecutors then claim Watson passed an object to Sansom, which was used to make cutting motions to Sharif's throat.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: The pair also deny wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, and unauthorised possession of two weapons in the form of a tin lid, and a pen attached to a handle.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Sara Sharif was killed in 2023 Judge Lynn Tayton KC set a two-week trial for 19 July, 2027, with pre-trial hearing set for June.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Urfan Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for murder, while his wife Beinash Batool, 30, received a minimum of 33 years.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Sara's uncle, Faisal Malik, 29, was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for causing or allowing her death.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: The three fled to Pakistan, with Sara's five siblings, the day before her body was found in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: They hid out there for four weeks before returning to the UK, where they were arrested.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Sara's siblings remain in Pakistan , where they have been living with their paternal grandfather.
sentences.article_title: Inmates deny attempt to murder Sara Sharif's father

sentences.text: Ofcom has launched an investigation into Pornhub owner, Aylo, over whether the site's new age checks are effectively stopping children from accessing adult content.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: The regulator said in May that Pornhub started using a new age verification process for some users, which relied on a third party, Apple.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: It said it had concerns that Aylo "may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing" before implementing this new process, and so it "may not be highly effective" at preventing children from seeing pornography.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: In a lengthy statement given to the BBC, Aylo strongly defended its system for age verification while stressing it would cooperate fully with the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA), sites that host pornographic material must use highly effective age assurance to ensure users are over 18, but it leaves it up to the service to decide the method of age-checking it will use.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Ofcom says as part of its investigation it will consider how Aylo implements its age verification processes and whether it conducted the "necessary due diligence" before it was implemented.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: It will not investigate how Apple operates its age checks.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: George Lusty, Ofcom's Director of Enforcement, said: "Online age checks are a vital protection to prevent children from encountering inappropriate or harmful material, including pornography.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: "We expect tech firms to ensure age checks are highly effective before introducing them.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Anything less could leave children at risk." But Aylo argues that, having experimented in multiple markets with multiple age-check methods, Apple's system "provides significantly stronger protection than any other age assurance method currently available in the UK market".
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: It also notes that Ofcom had previously praised Apple's technology as "a real win for children and families".
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Aylo argues a system based on asking individual pornographic sites to check users ages, simply drives users to riskier sites that aren't following Ofcom's rules.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Research by the Lucy Faithfull Foundation , external has previously suggested that non-compliant sites "may also be more likely to host harmful or illegal content, and in some cases, sexual images of children".
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: This probe is just the latest clash between the regulator and what is one of the world's most viewed porn sites.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: In October 2025 Pornhub said traffic from UK users had plunged by more than 75% following the introduction of more robust age checks by the OSA.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Some have questioned whether people were simply using Virtual Private Networks (VPN) to get around the checks instead.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: In January, Pornhub announced it would restrict access to its website in the UK, blaming the tougher checks, with only people who had previously made a Pornhub account able to access its content.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Aylo said that updates to the Act requiring age verification had "not achieved its goal of protecting minors".
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: However, in May, it said it would be making the site available again for some UK Apple users who had confirmed their age with the company's most up-to-date version of iOS, its mobile operating system.
sentences.article_title: Pornhub investigated over its age checks

sentences.text: Many farmers rely on government payments to manage their land in more environmentally-friendly ways Thousands of farmers missed out on vital government funding after online applications for a £233m green scheme for the whole of England closed down in under six hours.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Farming and environmental groups condemned the race to secure the sustainable farming incentive (SFI) funding, with some comparing it to a "frantic" online scramble to secure Glastonbury or Oasis gig tickets.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The post-Brexit scheme, which replaced EU subsidies with payments for farmers to look after nature and provide "public goods", opened at 10:00 BST on Tuesday but had run out of budget by 15:48 BST.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The government said farmers had responded "in force" to the scheme and there would be further funding opportunities for 2027.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The SFI scheme had been shut without warning last year so demand from farmers was expected to be high The National Farmers' Union (NFU) is calling for the government to explain why the scheme opened and closed so quickly, with so many farmers left out of pocket.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: It said it wanted "clarity and urgency" from the government and added that it had made "repeated warnings of a lack of sufficient budget".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: NFU vice-president Robyn Munt said: "The rapid uptake of the scheme comes as no surprise.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Its closure in less than six hours shows the scale of demand there is from farmers to deliver for the environment and to invest in farm resilience.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "The current cashflow pressures facing farmers and growers only exacerbates that demand as they look for certainty and clarity for the year ahead." Vicki Hird, agriculture lead at the Wildlife Trusts said "the scramble for green farming schemes was worse than the dash for Oasis tickets".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: When the scheme was suddenly closed without notice last year, there were concerns that some farmers might turn their backs on environmental work if they could not access the payments and demand for Tuesday's scheme was expected to be high.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN), which helps farmers to manage land in environmentally-friendly ways, criticised the "frantic scramble" and said farmers had "faced a desperate race against time" to secure their funding agreements.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Cambridgeshire arable farmer Martin Lines, who leads the NFFN, said: "This entire SFI system, with windows opening and closing within a few hours, isn't fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "We need to find a better way based on continuous, whole-farm agreements, not doors that slam shut on day one because the money has already gone." He pointed out that after years of extreme weather, many farmers were relying on the funding to help adapt their farms to climate change and become more resilient.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said it would provide further information on future opportunities for funding applications in 2027 "soon".
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: A Defra spokesperson said: "This year we ensured small farms and those new to SFI were prioritised - with an exclusive first window in the summer.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: "This is a scheme that works for farmers, backs food production, and delivers practical, sustainable land management, supporting the aims of our farming roadmap, our long-term plan for English farming," he said.
sentences.article_title: Farmers' fury as race for £233m funding compared to 'scramble for Oasis tickets'

sentences.text: Sandie Peggie gave evidence at an employment tribunal in Dundee A nurse has told an employment tribunal she did not believe her union representative took her objections to sharing female changing rooms with a transgender colleague as seriously as she did.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Sandie Peggie claims the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) failed to properly support and advise her after she was suspended over a complaint about her behaviour by Dr Beth Upton.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The RCN disputes the claim.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: It is the second employment tribunal Peggie has brought over the dispute with Upton – a transgender woman who was born biologically male.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie partially won a claim for harassment against NHS Fife in December last year, but her other allegations of discrimination and victimisation were dismissed.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The dispute began following a number of encounters between Peggie and Upton at the Victoria Hospital in Kirkcaldy towards the end of 2023.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The nurse was suspended shortly afterwards and spoke to RCN representative Stuart Fraser.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie said Fraser "appeared pleasant", explained how long a disciplinary process would last and said she should treat the leave "as an extended holiday".
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: "I thought he thought I'd been disciplined because I'd done something wrong." Peggie also said, after a meeting about her suspension, that she felt Fraser was "pushing" for her to change to another department against her wishes.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Asked how she felt, she replied: "Not supported.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: I feel like people were taking the doctor's side rather than mine." Cunningham also asked her client why certain members of staff did not give evidence during the first tribunal.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie said: "I think possibly it was fear.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: They had seen the way I had been treated from senior staff members." The first tribunal, against NHS Fife and Dr Upton, became a high profile and controversial case.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie was backed by the campaign group Sex Matters, co-founded by Maya Forstater.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The RCN's lawyer, David Hay KC, questioned Peggie about when she came to understand the phrase "gender critical".
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie said it would have been "round about" the time she spoke to Forstater, which was shortly after she contacted her MP in January 2024.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: "I was made aware that because of what had happened in the changing area, I didn't believe biological men should be in women's changing spaces.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The lawyer asked Peggie: "My reading is that the strategy is Sex Matters' strategy, as opposed to being a particular strategy from you?" She added that speaking with Forstater led her to understand that she had a legal case "because of my beliefs".
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Turning to contact between Peggie and the RCN union, Hay said the first time Peggie had put in writing that she felt "failed from the outset" by the union was in March 2025.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Prior to this, he said she had other opportunities to raise with her union representative that she was unhappy that the union had not offered her legal services.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie said: "I believe it [legal services] should have been offered." The tribunal heard that another RCN representative, Gillian Tait, took over Peggie's case from June 2025.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie said Tait had contacted her two or three times "just to check in".
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Hay said there had been "at least 11 occasions" when Tait was in contact with Peggie – during which the nurse opted not to meet or speak on the phone.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The lawyer said the union rep had offered opinions, kept Peggie in the loop, and demonstrated that she had sought assurances from the health board that Peggie would have access to single-sex spaces before returning to work.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Former MP Neale Hanvey put Peggie in touch with campaign groups Earlier in evidence, Peggie had said she did not believe the union had pushed NHS Fife to stop men accessing single-sex spaces for women, which Hay challenged.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Peggie conceded it "wasn't right" for her to say the union had not pushed at all.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: Former Alba MP Neale Hanvey, who also previously worked in cancer nursing, gave evidence to the tribunal.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: He said Peggie's mother had phoned his office about her case "because of my particular interest in sex and gender".
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: After meeting with the two women, Hanvey said it was "quite obvious" that Peggie was in a state of emotional distress and that she was not getting the support he would have hoped a union member would receive.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: He said he put Peggie in touch with the campaign groups Sex Matters and For Women Scotland because he felt it was "important that I used my connection with them" to provide the nurse with support.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The tribunal, which is taking place in Dundee, continues.
sentences.article_title: Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously

sentences.text: The future of Scotland's 32 council system hangs in the balance Council leaders have been voicing their concerns about proposals for the biggest shake up of local government in 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Some have warned that Scottish government plans to potentially streamline the number of authorities from 32 to six will not save money.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Others have questioned the potential impact on rural parts and the "absurd" timeline.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Under proposals for a new two-tier system , external , the regional bodies would focus on major issues such as education and economic growth.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Between 120 and 160 community authorities would also be created, contributing to  local issues such as licensing and town centre improvements.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Scotland's 32 councils could be cut to six under government plan The changes, which would fundamentally reshape a system that has existed since 1996,  have now been shared with Holyrood's committees and council umbrella body Cosla ahead of a public consultation.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: The Scottish government argues that some of these councils are too large to be truly local but too small to be strategic.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: For almost 20 years there has been talk of councils working together more closely to share overheads and cut duplication - for instance sharing responsibility for road maintenance or back office functions.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: But less has happened than had originally been expected and the talk now is of a fundamental overhaul.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Deputy First Minister Jenny Gilruth says the government wants to "empower communities" Deputy First Minister Jenny Gilruth has described the proposals as a "starting point" for reform.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: The old town councils - abolished in 1975 - which provided local services for distinct communities, sometimes of only a few thousand people.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: They worked together with county councils.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: There are no indications at present of the likely geographical boundaries of the new authorities.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Nor is there any indication of just how they would be funded.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Would the community bodies have tax raising powers of their own?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Or would the existing funding system be amended?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Inevitably this discussion may become intertwined with the question of replacing the council tax.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: So what do the current council leaders make of it?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Perth and Kinross Council leader Eric Drysdale wants to ensure the local authority has a "strong voice" in the debate Perth and Kinross Council will be one of the first to fully debate the proposals on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Council leader Eric Drysdale, told BBC Scotland News he wanted them to be "a starting point for discussion rather than any final decision".
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: He added: "We have valuable experience to contribute that other parts of Scotland could benefit from." Local authority workers help maintain roads But David Ross, leader of Fife Council , has questioned the very need for such fundamental structural reform - and does not think it will save money.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: He said it would be "much simpler and more effective" to maintain the status quo but allow local authorities to "merge if they wished" and to collaborate through city region and local growth deals.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Ross proposed that they should also be trusted to develop local arrangements for "community empowerment".
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: The council leader added: "Most local government services cannot simply be broken down into 'community areas' or they lose the economies of scale and operational efficiencies.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: One senior figure within Scottish local government that he thought the idea of six regions was simply a starting point or negotiating position.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: He thought around 10 would be more realistic.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Fundamental change costs money to begin with - any savings are achieved over the longer term.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Another council leader, Brian Connolly, who heads up South Ayrshire Council , wants the costs of reorganisation to be met by the Scottish government.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: He said: "The merits or otherwise of a regional approach can be debated but it is essential that local views and decision-making are maintained, along with substantial transfer of powers." Connolly added the three Ayrshire councils already have a "strong history of working together".
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Most of councils' revenue funding is used for day-to-day costs like road maintenance Given their proximity and links it is possible that Edinburgh, the three Lothian councils and the Scottish Borders could be within the same region.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: But Euan Jardine, leader of Scottish Borders Council , said: "My biggest concern is rural Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: "The Borders is a huge rural area made up of towns, villages and communities spread over a massive geography." He highlighted issues such as transport, access to services matters and local identity.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Jardine said: "The Scottish government has rightly recognised that island communities may need bespoke arrangements because geography matters.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: "Well, rural mainland Scotland deserves the same thinking.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: "You cannot take a model that might work in one part of Scotland and assume it will work everywhere else." The council leader said there were still "huge unanswered questions" in relation to local authority workers.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: He added: "Who employs people?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Who are they accountable to?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: What happens to existing council teams and local jobs?
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: None of that is clear yet." Edinburgh City Council leader Jane Meagher said many questions remained unanswered The leader of City of Edinburgh Council , Jane Meagher, also has questions and is worried the plan could be rushed through.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: She said it was unclear how community authorities would work and how they would be funded.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: Meagher told BBC Scotland News: "What this might mean for Edinburgh Council remains to be seen.
sentences.article_title: Council leaders wary of radical plan to redraw Scotland's local government map

sentences.text: On the other side of Scotland, Argyll and Bute is a geographically vast, rural council - stretching from the Glasgow commuter zone to tiny islands like Tiree and Iona.
