sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottle offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company Visit Toledo.

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: A new legal right to unpaid time off work after suffering a bereavement will cover step and half relatives, as well as foster, kinship care and adoptive relationships, the government has said.

sentences.text: From April next year, employees in Great Britain who lose a spouse, partner, parent, adult child or sibling will be entitled to up to two weeks' unpaid leave.

sentences.text: The government had already confirmed the new rights will also apply to parents who experience a miscarriage before 24 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.text: Previously only parents who have lost a child aged under 18 or stillborn from 24 weeks had a legal right to bereavement leave.
sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.text: Specialist courts to handle cases of rape and other sexual offences will be introduced across England and Wales over the next two years, the prime minister has announced.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Each crown court will have at least one courtroom set up to hear such cases, while alleged victims will be able to view proceedings remotely and give evidence from a separate room via video link.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: They will also be provided with private entrances and waiting rooms to separate them from defendants, though this will be dependent on the architecture of each building.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Rape Crisis England and Wales said this was a "significant step forward" that would introduce several reforms it had been requesting for years.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Taken together, they reflect the urgency of ensuring that courts are fit for purpose and properly meet the needs of victims and survivors, which is crucial to securing justice," the charity's chief executive, Ciara Bergman, said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Charities have complained that low prosecution rates for sexual offences and delays to court proceedings had disuaded victims from coming forward or pursuing justice.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Just 2.8% of rape offences recorded by police led to prosecutions in the year ending March 2024 and were the crimes that took the longest to investigate.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: A prior ONS study, using data from 2017-2020, suggested that only a sixth of the actual number of rape and attempted rape victims had reported their assault to the police, with more than a third saying this was because they felt the police could not help or that the process would be humiliating.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Victims minister Alex Davies-Jones said the new measures were part of efforts to bring down a backlog of Crown Court cases, which stood at 80,098 at the end of March.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Rape Crisis England and Wales said 15,373 of these cases - 19% - related to sexual offences.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Davies-Jones told BBC Breakfast that the introduction of specialist courtrooms "isn't enough on its own" to tackle the backlog and stressed the importance of the Courts and Tribunals Bill to improve "timeliness, effectiveness and also prevention".
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The Conservatives say the "long overdue" move should not come with restricting the number of jury trials, which is another provision of the bill.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Under the new measures, expected to cost around £23m of the Ministry of Justice's budget, court staff will also be given "trauma-informed training" and a single person of contact will be assigned to each survivor.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: From next month, trials will be given a fixed date rather than placed on floating lists in what Prime Minister Andy Burnham said was an effort to "rebalance the scales of justice and put victims first".
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: There are 84 crown court buildings across England and Wales, containing around 500 courtrooms, and Davies-Jones said the government was determined that every one of them would have at least one specialist rape and sexual offences courtroom by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Where architecture might prevent courtroom upgrades, Davies-Jones said staff would be expected to co-ordinate a "trauma informed approach" - for instance by scheduling different arrival times and rooms to give evidence from for victims and defendants.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The government said the changes follow Labour MP Charlotte Nichols showing "immense strength and bravery" in speaking publicly about being raped and calling for changes to the justice system.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Nichols waived her automatic right to anonymity in March when she made a Commons speech in which she described having to wait more than 1,000 days to go to court.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Labour promised in its 2024 manifesto to halve violence against women and girls within a decade.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "For too long, victims of rape and serious sexual offences have felt let down by our justice system," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Prosecution rates for rape remain shamefully low, with many victims waiting years for justice.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: This is not good enough." Nichols accused the then-Justice Secretary David Lammy of using victims as a "cudgel" to push through his reforms of the legal system when she spoke publicly for the first time about being raped.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: She was criticising the Courts and Tribunals Bill's plans to limit jury trials to cases with a likely prison sentence of three years or more.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage, doctors running a dedicated NHS clinic for it have told the BBC in an exclusive interview.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Medics at Alder Hey Hospital in Liverpool say some patients - they have had over 100 referrals since opening last May - describe "peeing a jellyfish", which is some of the bladder's protective lining being shed.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Prolonged damage can lead to incontinence or uncontrolled peeing, and even kidney failure.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Many children at the clinic had been taking ketamine for a year or more, meaning some may have started when they were 12 or younger.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Some with emotional trauma say the ketamine, sold for pocket money prices, helps "shush" or quieten their brain.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Ketamine's most common form is white or pale-brown grainy powder that is often inhaled (snorted) or sometimes injected by users.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: It can be a liquid or a crystal form too.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: The drug is a general anaesthetic so it reduces or blunts sensations in the body.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Users say it can make them feel dream-like and detached, chilled and relaxed.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: But it can also cause extreme harm.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Prof Rachel Isba who runs the clinic told the BBC some of the children she has seen had started wetting the bed or having to go to the toilet more often and in a hurry.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "Sometimes they don't always make it.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: They might have accidents...and a lot of them report pain in their bladder.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "They describe this feeling of weeing over broken glass.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: It's very painful." She says, unfortunately, some of them will use the ketamine to treat the pain.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "Ketamine is a very good pain reliever.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: It's an anaesthetic, and so they get into a vicious cycle or 'K loop', which makes their bladder worse," says Isba.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: She says ketamine is very cheap, "pocket-money level".
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "And you only need a small amount to feel an effect." She says some children find it hard to quit if their mates are still doing it.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "There's use going on at school.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: And, unfortunately for many of these children they are not able to attend education for various reasons." Some had pre-existing conditions like ADHD, while others had been in and out of the care system.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Ketamine abuse in children and young people is on the rise in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: The Alder Hey doctors , external saw one young patient in 2023, nine in 2024, and then "a rapid escalation" in 2025, which led them to open the bespoke clinic in May.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: They get about one referral every week from GPs or emergency departments in Cheshire, Merseyside and other nearby regions.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Of the first 60 they saw, 43 were girls.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Despite its name, "ketamine bladder" can affect the entire urinary tract, including the kidneys and ureters.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Symptoms include an urgent and frequent need to urinate.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: This can be very painful and the pee can be blood-stained.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Although stopping using ketamine can help, sometimes the damage can be so serious that the bladder needs surgical repair or even removal.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Some users experience abdominal pain and spasms, or "K cramps" too.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: There are reports that heavy users are getting liver damage, but it is difficult to separate harms from other things people may also be taking, including other street drugs and alcohol.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Isba says cannabis and alcohol are still more popular, but ketamine is "probably up into third place".
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Children at the clinic often say they have also tried other drugs, drank alcohol, and vaped.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: About three out of every 10 people who frequently use ketamine get bladder issues, says the British Association of Urological Surgeons , external .
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Sometimes it is reversible, if the drug use stops.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Given the risks, there have been calls to reclassify it as a Class A drug - like cocaine and heroin - but the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs has recommended to government that ketamine should remain a Class B controlled substance, like amphetamines and cannabis.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Isba says children are disadvantaged when it comes to accessing services.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: "There are definitely some children out there who are under the age of 16 who if they were 18 would be offered an inpatient detox stay.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: But because we don't have those facilities in the UK, they are not able to access that and that feels unfair.
sentences.article_title: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage

sentences.text: Twenty-year-old Anna-May manages on about five hours' sleep a night It's the start of university - you're already on your fourth themed night out of the week and have signed up for every quirky-sounding society your campus has to offer.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: But your relationship with your bed could be key to keeping up with a busy social life, as well as that lengthy reading list.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "If you can get out before 11am-ish then there's a part of the brain, just behind the eyes, that responds to light," says Jo Baker, a psychotherapist and student sleep and mental health expert.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "Getting daylight early on in the day is really going to help to keep your body in check.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: How you sleep at night starts with how you wake up in the morning." Sleep is essential to learning and absorbing information.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: But late nights out, noisy flatmates and a strange new bed can mean good sleep habits go out the window.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: She tries to stay awake during her commute to uni but admits sometimes "dosing off a bit" For Anna-May, 20, it's her four-hour round trip from Kendal, Cumbria to study dance at the University of Salford that leaves her short of sleep.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: She gets about five hours a night - the alarm goes at 05:00.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "I track my sleep and get worried about how little I will get, and then sometimes that keeps me up," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "I can tell I'm more tired towards the end of the week and things can feel harder." Forcing yourself to have an early night isn't going to work, according to Baker, especially if you end up lying wide awake in bed.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "Your brain learns this is somewhere I lie and get stressed about not being able to sleep - so the most important thing is a consistent waking time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: When you feel groggy, it's tempting to chug multiple coffees or fizzy drinks.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: But caffeine hangs around in the body and blocks the build-up of sleepiness throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Too many flat whites and you'll not only be short of cash - you could also develop a sleep problem.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Alcohol may also be a tempting way to boost your confidence around new people, but it doesn't help you sleep.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "When you fall asleep [after large amounts of alcohol], you're anaesthetised really.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: It's like having an anaesthetic.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: You're not asleep," Baker says.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: In fact, alcohol pushes out the deep sleep which restores you physically, and replaces it with lighter sleep, which doesn't.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Emma Young, deputy director of student services for health and wellbeing at Manchester Metropolitan University points out the low-key alternatives during freshers' week.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "There are lots of alcohol-free events now, like sip and paint.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Then the only way she can get to sleep is to watch episodes of Friends on her iPad.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: "I watch something I have seen time and time again - it's enough to quieten the busy part of my mind and I can fall to sleep," she says.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Anna-May, who is studying dance, accepts that watching TV before bed goes "against all the advice" But activities without screens like journalling or reading a book might be best for creating a calm, gradual transition to sleep.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Listening to music or a podcast can also work.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: The natural hormone melatonin rises before bedtime, making us feel sleepy.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: But watching social media reels or films means your eyes stay active, blocking that process and keeping you awake.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Freshers' flu is tricky to avoid , but good hand hygiene - washing regularly or using antibacterial hand gel - might just reduce your chances of getting a fever, sore throat and blocked nose, and spending a day or two in bed.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Meningitis is far more dangerous and requires urgent medical help (call 999).
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: It can look a lot like freshers' flu but if it's not diagnosed, it can progress very quickly and lead to seizures, brain damage and sepsis.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: That's why a free NHS vaccine called Men B is now on offer to all freshers students.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Many universities recommend planning ahead in case you feel ill and need some medical help at some point, especially if you're living away from home.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: A typical to-do list should include: Registering with a local GP Finding your nearest chemist Registering with an NHS dentist Finding out where the closest A&E is You might also want to check out what your uni has to offer in terms of mental health support.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Some pair up students for peer support and run dedicated 24-hour phone lines.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: Websites like Student Minds , external have lots of useful advice and information.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: And if you're not feeling like yourself, Young suggests a regular call home, to family or a best friend.
sentences.article_title: Fresh bedsheets and dusk walks: Expert tips for sleep-deprived freshers

sentences.text: The rule is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 at King's College Hospital in London in 2021 The NHS is expanding Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England to help patients and families challenge staff and seek a rapid review of their care if they want.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: It is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Her family's concerns were not listened to, which later prompted her parents, Merope and Paul, to change that culture by creating the rule.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Patients, loved ones and staff in A&E units will be able to call a dedicated phone number to trigger an urgent review if a patient's condition is deteriorating and they are concerned this is not being taken on board.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: The nationwide expansion should be complete by March 2028, after a trial at seven trusts.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: It is already being rolled out in all inpatient wards.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Scotland is beginning to use Martha's Rule and Northern Ireland is considering using it, while Wales has a similar scheme called Call4Concern.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: A coroner ruled , external in 2022 that Martha would probably have survived if she had been transferred earlier to intensive care and given appropriate treatment.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: She was in King's College Hospital in London after a cycling accident on a family holiday in which she fell heavily onto the handlebars after skidding on some sand.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: It left her with serious injuries to her pancreas.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: After a few weeks, she developed an infection and then signs of sepsis - when the body's response to an infection is overwhelming and ends up injuring its own tissues and organs - but this was not managed properly.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: The Crown actor Jason Watkins who lost his daughter Maude to sepsis spoke to the BBC about his support of Martha's law.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Prof Aidan Fowler, national director of patient safety at NHS England, said the expansion of Martha's Rule would give families and NHS staff "a critical new lifeline" to help improve care and save more lives.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: He told the BBC that a Martha's Rule call would mean a patient receives an "appropriate response" - for example, a senior nurse or member of the critical care outreach team could conduct a review of the case.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Staff can also ask for a review from a different team if they are concerned the appropriate action is not being taken.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Elliott Paterson, from Cheltenham, told the BBC he "truly believes" Martha's Rule saved the life of his 67-year-old father, Chris, who was treated at Gloucester Royal Hospital last year after he broke four ribs falling off his bike.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Elliott said his father's treatment in the surgical ward was complicated due to his Addison's disease, a rare autoimmune condition affecting the adrenal glands.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: The family noticed Chris' deterioration in health, Elliott said, and called the critical care team, which was then able to treat both Chris' injuries and his Addison's.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: "To hear that Martha's Rule is now to be rolled out across the NHS is brilliant news and I hope that for more people it will continue to save lives," Elliott said.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: "I am incredibly fortunate and grateful to have had Martha's Rule at our disposal at the time." During an eight-month pilot of the scheme at seven emergency departments, 69 calls were made to dedicated Martha's Rule phone numbers, including some calls relating to acute deterioration following an urgent clinical review.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: In some cases, it led to a patient having immediate surgery or being transferred to intensive care.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Fowler told the BBC's Today programme that, while these numbers might seem relatively small, the decision to roll out Martha's Rule further was "on a background of very, very extensive experience in other settings".
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: This included in-patient wards, where he said his teams had received "nearly 20,000 calls" - three quarters of which came from families.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: "Actually people have used it very sensibly," he added.
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: "We've tested it through winter and across this busy summer, and therefore I am not concerned that when we roll this out we are going to be overwhelmed with calls." Health minister Baroness Merron said the initiative was part of "wider efforts to put patient safety at the heart of the NHS".
sentences.article_title: Martha's Rule rolled out at every A&E department in England

sentences.text: Actor Jason Watkins, whose two-and-a-half-year-old daughter Maude died from sepsis in 2011, praised the rollout, saying Martha's Rule was already "making a difference on the wards".

sentences.text: Scientists say they have discovered why the bacteria responsible for the UK's worst outbreak of meningitis B in Kent earlier this year proved so dangerous.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: More than 20 young people, mostly students, were infected in the March outbreak , linked to a Canterbury nightclub.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: All needed hospital treatment, while nine ended up in intensive care and two died.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Experts at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and the University of Oxford, who have looked at the DNA of the bacterium , external , say it picked up some genetic material from other bugs found naturally in the throats of some people.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: This exchange created a new strain or variant that then spread between clubbers and caused severe illness.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Experts stress the meningitis vaccine currently being offered to more than a million young people starting university protects against it.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Young people can book to get their Men B vaccine at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: There are walk-in appointments too , external .
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Two doses offer the best protection.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: First doses are available until 31 December 2026, with second doses available until 31 March 2027.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Dr Charlene Rodrigues, consultant in Pathogen Genomics at UKHSA, said: "This investigation shows just how quickly and dramatically these bacteria can change.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: "The fact this outbreak variant was able to spread to so many young people was due to the social environment, a place where lots of close social mixing takes place." Speaking exclusively to the BBC, she said bacteria are known to undergo changes like this, known as horizontal gene transfer.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Such changes can make infections more severe, and may mean they get past the immune system because people haven't encountered them before.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: These events, while rare and unpredictable, could happen again, so experts "should not take their eye off the ball", she added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Scientists say speed and severity of the Kent outbreak was very unusual .
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: It was described as "unprecedented" and "explosive" at the time, with so many infections happening in one place and over a very short period.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Two people died - a 21-year-old University of Kent student and Juliette Kenny, a sixth-form pupil at Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School in Faversham.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: The outbreak is thought to have started in a nightclub called Club Chemistry in the city centre, which was popular with university students.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: It's likely one person brought the infection in with them, and then it spread that evening.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Meningitis is passed through close contact - including kissing and sharing drinks or vapes.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Dr Rodrigues suspects the very same genetic changes that made the strain so dangerous may also explain why the outbreak was short-lived and did not continue to spread.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: People were generally too sick to be silent carriers who can pass it on unknowingly to others.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Prof Robert Heyderman, an expert in infectious diseases at University College London, said the outbreak strain could have been carried by healthy people for some time before the conditions were right for the outbreak to occur.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Following the Kent outbreak, a one-off menB vaccination programme was launched to protect young people heading to university this autumn.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Advisers are asking the government to consider introducing MenB jabs routinely for secondary school-aged people at around the age of 15 to better protect them against a disease that can be deadly.

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts
