sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Periods of hot weather can affect anyone, but some people run a greater risk of serious harm.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This, combined with the lowered blood pressure, can lead to heat exhaustion.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Symptoms include: If blood pressure drops too far, the risk of heart attacks rises.

sentences.text: Staying safe in water when the weather's hot Our bodies strive to keep a core temperature of about 37C whether we are in a snowstorm or a heatwave.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: That is the temperature at which our bodies have evolved to work.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: But as the weather gets hotter, it is harder for the body to keep its core temperature down.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: It opens more blood vessels near the skin to lose heat to our surroundings and starts sweating.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the sweat evaporates, it dramatically increases the heat lost from the skin.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: No one - especially babies, young children and animals - should ever be left in a locked vehicle.

sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Their temperature could go over 40C and they might have seizures or lose consciousness.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Those living in top-floor flats will also face higher temperatures.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Yes - but the NHS says people should keep taking their medication as normal, and focus on staying cool and hydrated.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diuretics - sometimes called "water pills" - increase the amount of water the body expels.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: They are taken widely, including for heart failure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Antihypertensives - which lower blood pressure - can combine with the blood vessels that are dilating to cope with the heat and cause dangerous drops in blood pressure.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Some drugs for people with epilepsy and Parkinson's can block sweating and make it harder for the body to cool itself.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Other drugs such as lithium or statins can become more concentrated and problematic in the blood if there is too much fluid loss.

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This could be because we start to change our day-to-day behaviour as summer progresses and we get more used to dealing with the heat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.

sentences.text: A common symptom of the menopause is a hot flush Partners of women going through the menopause are being invited to experience one of the symptoms at a forthcoming support event.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: At the Menopaus'ull Support Network event in Hull next month, health group Over The Bloody Moon will be taking one of its MenoVests, allowing people to experience a hot flush – one of the symptoms of the menopause.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Sarah Weichardt, who co-manages the project, said: "We're particularly interested in getting men along to come and experience the MenoVest, just so that they can understand what women go through." The event will be at Princes Quay shopping centre on 17 October, from 10:30 until 14:30 BST.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "It's not just a hot flush, it's what the hot flush brings with it," said Weichardt.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "So it could be panic, it could be anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: It's experiencing it all at the same time." She said she hoped the vest would give people a "better understanding of what women are going through".
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "The more people we can get to experience it, the better," she added.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The menopause describes the end of a woman's reproductive years, and often happens at about the age of 50.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The period leading up to this is called the perimenopause, which is when many women notice their periods becoming unpredictable.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Other symptoms can include mood shifts, difficulty sleeping, and discomfort during sex.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Weichardt said her organisation had a banner with nearly 40 symptoms on it.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Many women "don't necessarily know that they're going into the menopause or they're perimenopausal" until they see the banner – and then they sometimes have a "lightbulb moment", she said.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Once women have "accepted it and are happy" they are menopausal or peri-menopausal, they can seek the support they need, she added.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: There is also a Menopaus'ull Support Network event in Beverley on 10 October between 10:30 and 13:30 BST at the Toll Gavel Church.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.

sentences.text: Schools had been expected to fund some of the 3.5% teachers pay increase for the current school year out of their existing budgets, which National Education Union (NEU) leaders had strongly objected to.

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The additional money could potentially bring the uplift for this year into line with next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Kebede said schools has been "running on empty" and the funding signalled "a welcome return to reality, and a message of hope for the entire school community".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Similarly, the NASUWT union welcomed the news.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Renewables make up for 54% of India's total 552GW installed power capacity On a hot July afternoon this year, electricity generated from renewable energy briefly met over half of India's peak power demand - only the second time this happened.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: The first instance was around the same period a year ago.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: While it was only briefly that power generated from solar, wind, hydro and nuclear sources collectively outstripped coal-based output, it was a milestone moment reflecting the astonishing growth of non-fossil fuels to the country's electricity mix over the last decade.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: "It showed that renewable energy is no longer a marginal source sitting at the edge of the power system," Sumant Sinha, CEO of ReNew Power, one of India's largest Nasdaq-listed clean energy companies, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: To be sure, coal-based power plants still continue to generate 70% of India's electricity on average because they run on a higher load factor, or for more hours than solar or wind.

sentences.text: Yet, the country's push for clean energy appears to have reached a crucial inflection point.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: For a nation long seen as the poster child for dirty coal dependence, this rapid transition points to a remarkable achievement in decarbonising its grid.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Yet, the gains are tempered by some serious challenges.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Electricity generated from renewable energy briefly met over half of India's peak power demand in July Foremost among them is a shortage of grid capacity.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: The renewables' build out has significantly outpaced transmission infrastructure, a point of major concern for policymakers.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: "In the first quarter of 2026, transmission constraints accounted for nearly two-thirds of all renewable energy curtailment at 300 gigawatt-hours (GWh)," according to Ember, a global energy think-tank.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Put simply, that means a bulk of the clean energy that was produced in India was wasted because the country's transmission lines have been dogged by missed targets, with one out of four inter-state projects facing delays of over a year.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: The difficulty lies in matching the speed of generation projects with the grid build-out, says Sinha.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: "Generation projects can be constructed in 18-24 months… Transmission can take much longer because they involve right-of-way, land acquisition, approvals and coordination across many agencies.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: It is an execution issue that becomes more important as the system gets larger," he adds.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Vibhuti Garg of the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis also blames "poor planning" for the problem.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: The grid was able to absorb new capacity as long as India was generating 10-15GW annually, she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: But that pace has dramatically increased, reaching a record 51GW last year, and the infrastructure is no longer able to cope.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: The concentration of renewables projects in the north-western states of Gujarat and Rajasthan has also compounded the challenge of evacuating power in the face of such grid shortages.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Analysts at Ember now believe this growing mismatch between fast-moving generation projects and slower-moving transmission infrastructure, is the "most critical operational risk to the country's 2030 target of 500 gigawatts (GW) of non-fossil electricity".
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: A quick solution to addressing this gap would have been to build battery storage systems at renewable pooling stations to integrate the power into the grid.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: But storage capacity has not grown because of a huge jump in the price of batteries, raw material shortages due to the war in the Middle East and a fall in the value of the Indian currency which has jacked up financing costs for Indian companies.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: "Many storage projects that were meant to come up fell through as a result," Garg adds.
sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: While ample global capital is available for green transition across the developed world, getting access to it remains a persistent struggle for Indian clean energy companies, despite the strides that the country has made in its renewables commitments.

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Plugging these critical gaps in finance, transmission infrastructure and storage will be critical given this transition is under way at a pivotal moment, say experts.

sentences.article_title: India is producing more green energy - but wasting a lot of it

sentences.text: Wildfires fuelled by El Niño are affecting around 12.5 million people across Indonesia, according to the country's health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The developing El Niño climate phenomenon is now the strongest on record, according to scientists monitoring Pacific Ocean temperatures.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Daily sea surface temperatures in a key region of the central-eastern Pacific were 3.05C above average on 19 September - exceeding the previous record of 3.02C set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Some longer-term measures of El Niño have not yet hit record levels but this is likely to change, with the peak not expected until later this year.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño can cause major shifts in weather patterns around the world, with the Met Office saying many of the expected impacts are already being felt.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office What is El Niño and why could it mean record temperatures?
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Heat is then released from the ocean into the atmosphere which can boost global temperatures and drive changes in weather patterns around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Forecasters track the development of El Niño by watching temperatures in a key region of the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: When these are consistently 0.5C above normal, an El Niño is declared.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: There are different ways of measuring the strength of El Niño, however.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The records that have now been broken relate to daily measurements of sea surface temperature compared with the long term historical average.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This is called the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Many scientists - including forecasters in the USA and Australia - also consider an alternative measure known as the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This measures how warm the key El Niño region is relative to the rest of the tropical oceans, meaning it takes into account the background warming caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: By the RONI index the current El Niño is not yet a record-breaker - but it is likely that more announcements will follow in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Adam Scaife, Head of Long Range Prediction at the Met Office, said: "We have been signalling for months that the developing El Niño will be an unprecedented event.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: "The fact that it has already exceeded previous records – with several weeks to go before it peaks later this year – shows the enormity of this El Niño." Every El Niño is different, therefore impacts on global weather patterns are not guaranteed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: And the unprecedented strength of this El Niño does not necessarily mean it will have unprecedented impacts on the weather.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Scaife said: "Scientists are still assessing whether the impacts will be in proportion to its magnitude, but we are already seeing expected effects worldwide." El Niño increases the odds of storms and floods in some regions and of drought and wildfires in others.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: How does El Niño affect world weather?
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño years tend to bring below-average monsoon rainfall in India, which is already being reflected in this year's data.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Statistics from the India Meteorological Department show that, until 22 September the southwest monsoon had brought 15% less rain than normal.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Another typical impact of El Niño is reduced hurricane activity in the Atlantic due to changes in wind patterns high in the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: So far in 2026 there have been no Atlantic hurricanes, setting a new record for the latest date without a hurricane forming since satellite monitoring of storms began.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Other possible effects - some of which are already being felt - include the increased risk of floods in coastal parts of Ecuador, Peru and the southern USA, and the enhanced threat of drought and wildfires in Brazil, Australia and Indonesia.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: These weather impacts can have significant knock on effects for on crop yields, food security and economies around the globe.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The UK is thousands of miles from the tropical Pacific and so the effects of El Niño tend to be less clear-cut than in other regions.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: However, it does bring the increased chance of wet and stormy conditions across north-west Europe during the late autumn and early winter.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: A forecast released by the Met Office this autumn stated that there were already "signals for increased rainfall and storminess in autumn here in the UK", especially into November and December.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The winter of 2015 and 2016, which coincided with a very strong El Niño, brought a succession of major storms delivering what experts at the time described as the most extreme flooding on record.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: In addition to storminess, El Niño can also be associated with UK cold spells in the late winter - but the link is not a strong one and the past evidence is mixed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The so-called Big Freeze of winter 2009/2010 was, at the time, the coldest in three decades - and this coincided with an El Niño.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: However, 2006/2007 was also an El Niño winter and that was unseasonably warm.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: As this unprecedented El Niño approaches its likely peak towards the end of 2026, scientists will continue to monitor its development - and its impact on weather around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This video can not be played Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ From behind a giant bank of screens in a small windowless room, Estelle Morgan, animal team leader from the Saving Wildcats partnership, is keeping an eye on the latest wildcats being bred in captivity for release into the Cairngorms.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: "It's like Big Brother for cats", she says of the 72 cameras being used to watch over the animals in their enclosures.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: They are assessing whether they're healthy and have the behavioural potential to survive in the wild.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: "We want to know what the cats are actually doing," she says.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Estelle Morgan monitors the wildcats via 72 cameras in the Cairngorms "What are they like without us there? she adds.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Can they navigate complex structures?
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Are they active at natural times?" This year they were even able to capture on camera for the first time a wildcat giving birth.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: It is quite a surveillance programme - but it has to be.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Seventy-two cameras are being used to watch over the animals in their enclosures They don't want the cats to become comfortable around people and contact is kept to an absolute minimum.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: They are also assessing the cats' behaviour ahead of being released: "If we've got some cats which are quite bold does that mean they're more likely to go near roads in the wild, or venture closer to a farm or to human settlements," she says.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: For the first time this year, Saving Wildcats were able to observe a wildcat having its kittens Saving Wildcats has been successful in reintroducing 46 wildcats into the flats and foothills of the Cairngorms .
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Those wildcats have successfully reproduced and the team working on the project are aware of at least 20 wild-born litters to released females since 2024.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: There are now plans to reintroduce wildcat populations into other areas in Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: The Cairngorm project has had "an enormous amount of success, but it is only the first step," says NatureScot species project manager Dr Martin Gaywood.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Now he says they need to think big: "Wildcat conservation is really complex.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Helen Senn said climate incidents had the potential to have an impact on the wildcat conservation programme As well as identifying new release sites, the national strategy will prioritise restoring and reconnecting wildcat habitats to allow the expansion of their range.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: In the areas chosen for the eventual translocation of wildcat populations there will be additional microchipping, neutering and vaccination of pet and feral cats to reduce interbreeding.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Dr Helen Senn, head of conservation and science at the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland (RZSS), says climate change is one of the reasons why is it important to  identify other areas in which wildcat populations can be reintroduced.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: "We have had some really big climate incidents here in the Strath over the last couple of years.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: "We've had some major storms and flooding incidents.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: We've also had, unfortunately, a very significant forest fire in the north of the release area and all of these have the potential to impact the population".
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: She adds: "The way to be resilient to risk is to have larger population sizes and to have populations present in multiple areas".
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: They are classed as critically endangered so even once released the wildcats that now roam the Cairngorms are still carefully monitored.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: It can also help them understand the habitat the wildcats are using.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Several estates have been actively helping: providing release sites, monitoring the wildcats, recording sightings.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: Louise takes me to the territory on which one wildcat that was recently captured on camera:  "The cat that lives in this territory, Sully, is an amazing cat.
sentences.article_title: Inside Scotland's wildcat HQ - 'It's like Big Brother for cats'

sentences.text: She was released in 2024 and she has been captured on video swimming across the River Spey." Wildcats, she says, "never cease to surprise us." Estelle Morgan points out that wildcats were once widespread throughout the UK.

sentences.text: The work they are doing in the Cairngorms will help inform releases elsewhere in Scotland.

sentences.text: The glutinous snail was once widespread in the UK, but is now only found in one Welsh lake A rare snail found in just one lake in the UK started laying eggs on its six-hour journey from Wales to Kent, as a zoo joined a nationwide effort to save the species.

sentences.text: Glutinous snails are no bigger than a fingertip and used to be widespread across UK water ways.
sentences.article_title: Rare snails lay eggs during car journey to zoo

sentences.text: It is thought habitat disruption and environmental changes reduced their population to such an extent that they are only now found in Llyn Tegid , a lake in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia.

sentences.text: Wingham Wildlife Park near Canterbury has taken some of the wild population to breed and release into the wild.

sentences.text: The BBC's defence correspondent explains what the US announcement means The announcement by the United States that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth's orbit has raised questions about what weaponry is actually in space, and what role it could play in efforts by great powers to dominate that arena.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Washington has given away little in its announcement.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the "on orbit" weapon was necessary to safeguard US forces against hostile enemy action, but gave no details about the weapon's capabilities or when it was put into orbit.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: So what could this weapon be, and what is the wider picture like for military developments in space?
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Who else could have similar weaponry?
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Space has been a militarised domain since the start of the space age - in the late 1960s, the Soviet Union deployed weapons up there.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: The Istrebitel Sputnikov (IS; Satellite Destroyer) programme was made up of satellites that were designed to release projectiles that detonated, releasing shrapnel into the path of another (usually American) satellite.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Nowadays, advanced militaries deploy satellites in space for a range of purposes, including reconnaissance, secure communications, detecting missile launches and providing precise location information for targeted strikes.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: As warfare becomes more technologically advanced, analysts expect the use of military hardware in space to increase.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Some types of space weaponry could create a lot of debris and destruction Dr Bleddyn Bowen, an associate fellow in military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute and associate professor in astropolitics at Durham University, said he was only able to hazard a guess about the weapon announced by the US.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "I would expect there to be some kind of electronic warfare or radio-jamming platform, possibly, this would be a non-destructive kind of anti-satellite weapon," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Such weaponry already exists on Earth and can disrupt satellite communications, he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "If you take out the radio links then your satellite is very useless." Bowen also would not rule out a riskier and more disruptive type of weaponry, which could create debris and destruction.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "Less likely would be a kinetic kill vehicle of some sort, so a vehicle that would release a projectile that could ram into a satellite and destroy it," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: A type of "close inspection and grappling satellite would be another possibility as well." As to whether rivals such as Russia and China have similar weaponry already in orbit, is difficult to tell.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "If we're looking towards China and Russia, they have both displayed activity," Juliana Suess, a former research fellow at RUSI and researcher at the Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik (German Institute for International and Security Affairs), told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "For example, with Russia, we've seen some activity that hints at being a co-orbital weapons test.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: So we saw something that might indicate that they shot a projectile as a test in orbit.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: In a later BBC interview, Bowen was dismissive of China's reaction to the US announcement which warned against an arms race in space, describing it as "the pot calling the kettle black".
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "If you're already an expert... you know how hollow those words are coming from the Russian and Chinese governments," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "The United States, Russia and China and also India have all developed different kinds of anti-satellite or counter-space weapons, and Russia and China have put a lot of technologies in space which have a lot of weapons potential," he added.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: In fact in the past 10 years, Russia and China have been doing a lot more manoeuvres in space, known as rendezvous and proximity operations (RPOs) - "buzzing" Western satellites.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "Theoretically, these RPO [satellites]can become hunter-killer satellites by physically colliding with them or by nudging them out of orbit," Dr Rod Thornton, reader in Russian Defence and Security Studies at King's College, London, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Bowen added that the Chinese have demonstrated "space tug capability", saying: "A vehicle can go up to a satellite, can grapple it and move it into a different orbit." This, he said, could be a positive development - a way of removing space junk as well as knocking out working satellites.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: However, some types of space weaponry also have the potential to create huge amounts of space junk.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Dr Mark Hilborne, a specialist in space security and weaponisation at King's College,  said direct ascent anti-satellite missile tests, such as one carried out by China in 2007, leave a great deal of debris in orbit for a very long time.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Suess said debris from that test was still in orbit and still dangerous.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "It doesn't have to be a sort of huge piece of metal to do any damage, it can be a tiny piece of plastic, given the velocity that we're talking about in orbit," she said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Thornton said that what Russia lacks in space weaponry and satellites, it makes up for in missile capability.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "The Russians... have ground-based missiles which can be launched into space to strike [satellites] in low Earth orbit.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: They also have ASAT [air-launched antisatellite] missiles that can be launched from a great height by aircraft," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Only if it was happening on the ground as well.

sentences.text: The BBC understands that Nepal hopes to claim around $20m (£15m) from the UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which helps countries affected by climate change.

sentences.text: Around 1,400 people have died in the disaster while 6,150 people remain missing in Nepal as of Wednesday, according official data.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The study by research group World Weather Attribution, published on Thursday, says climate change was a likely contributing factor in the avalanche of rock and ice that unleashed devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border last month.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: There was "absolutely no doubt that human-induced climate change played a role here in the preconditioning of the disaster", said Dr Friederike Otto, an Imperial College London climatologist who co-authored the study.
