sentences.text: Massive floods and landslides swept through border towns and villages in Nepal and Tibet, wiping out thousands of houses, destroying energy infrastructure and leaving thousands dead or missing.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Scientists say the floods were caused by a collapse of rock wall and glacier ice near the peak of Langtang Lirung, a mountain on Nepal's side of the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The study said the disaster was the result of a "compound event" caused by rising temperatures, thinning glaciers, thawing permafrost and pre-existing geological weaknesses According to the study, July and August temperatures in the area were around 1.5C (2.7F) warmer "due to human influence on the climate".
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Meanwhile, glaciers in the region had also been thinning by about half a metre (1.6ft) a year, which could weaken existing fractures and increase instability.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Heavy snowfall last October and November also added to a large amount of meltwater early this year.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Climate change, while not the only cause of the disaster, was a "destabilising factor acting on a pre-existing geological predisposition", the study said.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: In the wake of the floods, Nepal's leaders have said the country needs around $5bn (£3.7bn) to rebuild itself.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: The UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, which came into operation last year, requires countries to submit evidence proving that the losses they faced were caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: Nepali officials had been preparing satellite and drone images, as well as preliminary reports, to back up its request to the fund.
sentences.article_title: Nepal to use new flood study to claim millions from UN climate disaster fund

sentences.text: But the World Weather Attribution report is now the strongest evidence for their claim that climate change was a significant factor in the collapse of rock and ice at  Langtang Lirung, authorities say.

sentences.text: The report "will be the main basis of our claim as it has detailed what role climate has played in this disaster," said Maheshwar Dhakal, spokesperson for Nepal's Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment.

sentences.text: FoodNeverComes calls itself a 'dopamine kitchen' You are hungry.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: You open FoodNeverComes, pick from 22 cuisines and start scrolling.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Butter chicken looks good.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: You add a few dishes, watch the total climb and hit checkout.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: A tracker says a rider is on the way.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Then you get a dummy AI-generated call from inside the site.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: He is outside your building, he says, but cannot find your street or door.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Except there was never any food in the first place.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: The order exists only on the screen.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: It now offers 22 kitchens, 327 dishes and 319 real recipes, complete with fake prices, a simulated checkout and a fictional delivery experience.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: The site offers 22 fake kitchens, 327 dishes and 319 real recipes FoodNeverComes belongs to a new internet genre: "dopamine sites", which recreate the rituals of consumption without the consumption.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: There are fake shopping sites, fake delivery services and even fake holidays.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: The genre took off in South Korea , external and has since travelled well beyond, spawning a growing crop of sites - Dopamine Shop , external or Fakehaul , external , for example - that mimic everything from food delivery and shopping to travel.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: What, exactly, are we enjoying when we enjoy buying something?
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: The idea began with the founders' own shopping habits.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Parmar and Sharma met on a computer science diploma course and later started NeuroX AI, which builds software and AI products and makes Instagram content.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: They noticed it in their own lives: online baskets filling up with things they wanted, but never actually bought.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Sharma would browse electronics, fill an online basket and abandon it.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Parmar's mother did much the same.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "She would add things to the cart and say, 'I will order this later'," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Parmar's own version ended at food delivery checkouts.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: During a two-month project in Mumbai, he says, he was spending 5,000-10,000 rupees a week on food, sometimes ordering treats he did not necessarily need: Belgian waffles, ice cream and, once, a large jar of sour cream he barely wanted and gave away to friends.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: He believes "perhaps the real craving was not always for the food, but for the ritual of ordering it".
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Purvansh Parmar says he spent a lot of money on a work trip on food and treats he did not necessarily need What begins as genuine hunger, the two argue, can become associated with the pleasure of ordering.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Over time, boredom, anxiety or habit can trigger the urge even when the hunger has disappeared.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "Sometimes you're not hungry at all.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: You're bored or busy, and then you realise that ordering food makes you feel good.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: You start associating the act of ordering with that dopamine hit.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Eventually, it's not just the food you want," says Parmar.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Ravi Dhar, director of the Yale Center for Customer Insights, calls this "anticipatory utility" - the pleasure of looking forward to consumption.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: It is especially strong with things that capture the imagination - a new pair of shoes, a holiday, a restaurant meal - because anticipation becomes part of the experience.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Sometimes, Dhar says, anticipation can be more pleasurable than ownership: "The thrill is in the chase." Once the object is acquired and the tension resolved, psychological arousal falls.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Neuroscience has a name for this gap between the chase and the catch, and it complicates a popular idea.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Dopamine is not simply the brain's pleasure chemical, whatever the internet's talk of "dopamine hits" might suggest.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Swiggy, a popular food delivery site in India, alone handled roughly 2.5m consumer orders a day in FY2025 Kent Berridge, a University of Michigan neuroscientist who developed the theory of "wanting" and "liking", says they are separate processes.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Wanting is the motivational pull towards something; liking is the pleasure of having it.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: They often travel together, but not always.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Dopamine, in his account, drives the first, not the second.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Tempting food or products online are likely to activate this wanting system, which Berridge calls "incentive salience".
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "Some situations can trigger 'wanting' by itself," he says.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: We can pursue something intensely even when the eventual pleasure is weak - or, in more everyday terms, want something more than we ultimately like it.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Dr Anna Lembke, a Stanford University addiction psychiatrist and author of Dopamine Nation, makes a similar distinction.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "To call dopamine a chemical of pleasure is an oversimplification," she told me.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "Dopamine is the molecule that says 'get more of' or 'do more of', but it doesn't necessarily equate to pleasure." TripNeverLeaves lets users plan a holiday before sending them on a virtual flight that never leaves the runway.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: What she adds is the role of ritual.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Cues and habits attached to a reward can become reinforcing in their own right, she says: in addiction, the routines leading up to drug use can eventually matter as much as the drug itself.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "Anticipation of reward can be as reinforcing as the reward itself," she says.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Can repeatedly ordering imaginary food satisfy a real craving?
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Berridge says the ritual could produce a "dopamine hit and strong 'wanting', and also evoke faint conditioned 'liking'".
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: But he would expect the "novelty to soon wear off", and would be "surprised" if many people returned to place more than about 10 imaginary orders.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Dhar is more open to the possibility that simulated consumption could serve as a kind of release valve.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "While we still need more empirical data to know if simulated shopping can satisfy a consumer urge, evidence from simulated consumption in gaming shows it can be highly effective," he says.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: A festive sale of of e-commerce site in India featuring Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan But there is an equally plausible danger: the ritual may simply rehearse the behaviour it is supposed to replace.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: Lembke says the evidence is not in yet, and the effect may depend on the person.
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: But her own bet is that, over time, the sites could "reinforce the same addictive neural networks they are trying to simulate".
sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: "The one up side, though, is that people using these sites have on some level already admitted to themselves they have a problem, and that admission is often the first step in recovery," says Lembke.

sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.article_title: Indians are discovering the thrill of shopping without paying

sentences.text: The tech giant OpenAI will share its AI cyber defence system Daybreak for free with the Ukraine government to help it protect civilian infrastructure, like hospitals and power plants, from cyber-attacks.

sentences.text: Daybreak is able to quickly identify weaknesses in digital systems and help develop fixes.

sentences.text: Under the deal, Ukraine will get access to OpenAI's advanced GPT 5.6 Sol model - a rival to Anthropic's Mythos and Fable.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.text: "Any initiative that strengthens Ukraine's already highly capable, but heavily burdened, cyber defence efforts is a welcome development and could provide a valuable force multiplier," he said.

sentences.text: Jamie MacColl, a senior research fellow specialising in cyber at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), told the BBC western tech firms had been supporting Ukraine for some time - partly for altruistic reasons but also because they gain very valuable data and intelligence from an active conflict.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.text: "Given this, it's no surprise that OpenAI is now also providing defensive cyber security services" he said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.text: The cyber-abilities of the latest, most powerful AI models, called "frontier" models in AI jargon, can be a boon for cyber-defenders, but the same abilities can also be used for attack.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

sentences.text: Under Australia's draft digital duty of care laws, tech firms risk hefty fines if they fail to give users the option to turn off algorithms in a bid to protect them from harmful content.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: In a rare submission to the proposed laws, the US embassy in Canberra said it had "serious concerns" and allowing the government to "enforce vague definitions of 'harm'" would lead to "viewpoint-based censorship".
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the legislation was not about giving governments control but giving it back to individuals.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: "We ask that Australia clarify how exactly 'harm' and 'risks' shall be determined... ensuring these definitions do not encroach on protected speech," the US said in its submission.

sentences.text: The US also claimed that the proposed laws may risk "reducing the reach of independent journalists or other voices whose content touches on sensitive or controversial topics" if tech firms had to "pre-emptively demote" them.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: An opt-out option would "allow regulators to impose rigid, one-size-fits-all platform design requirements" on tech firms and this could affect users outside of Australia, it said.
sentences.article_title: US criticises Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'

sentences.text: Another worry was that the proposed laws could affect Australia's "reputation as a jurisdiction that enables innovation," the submission said.

sentences.text: The criticism comes during Albanese's visit to the US to speak at the UN's General Assembly about his government's tech policies.

sentences.text: England beat Spain 5-1 in the final of the Transplant World Cup in Frankfurt When Martyn Jackson walked off the pitch after Ramsbottom United's 2-1 win over Cheadle Town in October 2024, it never crossed his mind that one day he could be a World Cup winner.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: In fact, in the days after that match, his goal was just staying alive.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Just a couple of days after the final whistle, Jackson started to feel unwell during the night.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: He went into hospital and was diagnosed with myocarditis, an inflammation of the heart usually caused by an infection.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Within weeks, he was placed on the super urgent waiting list for a transplant.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: His life was saved when a donor heart became available, and on 28 November 2024, he had successful surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital in Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Fast forward to September 2026, and Jackson scored for England in their 5-1 win over Spain in the final of the Transplant Football World Cup.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: His team-mates and opponents were, like him, all recipients of a donor organ.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: This video can not be played England's win at the Transplant World Cup came three days before the start of Organ Donation Week "Obviously, when you've had a transplant, you don't think you're ever going to play again.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: That's what I thought anyway," Jackson tells BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "I'll be forever grateful to my donor and the family for what they've given me.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: They've given me the gift of life and the opportunity to live my life to the fullest." Football at the Transplant World Cup is not quite the same as the game played at the Fifa World Cup.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Instead, it reflects how delicate each player's body is having been through life-altering surgery.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Matches are seven-a-side and played over 20-minute halves.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Contact is "not as aggressive as I was used to", Jackson says.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Having played 11-a-side football in the ninth tier of English football before his surgery, he became a game-changing new addition to the national transplant team when he joined up with the squad in January 2026.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Jackson spent his youth career in the academy at Manchester United, before spells at Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Burnley.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: He eventually stopped pursuing a career as a professional and spent 13 years with clubs across the non-league pyramid.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: During his recovery, wife Lucy heard about the opportunity to join an England Transplant FC team on social media.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Martyn Jackson won the Transplant World Cup less than two years after receiving a new heart Daley Cross, manager of the England team, said of Lucy's role: "She was just trying to do her best for him and trying to find a way to motivate him.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "His wife did drop in the conversation that he used to play at Manchester United as a schoolboy.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: So that got our ears twitched instantly.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "You could tell from him being on the pitch, even though he was so fresh into his journey, that he knew the football game and he would be such an incredible asset to us.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "You can be in a dark place, at the time of diagnosis, through your treatment or even post-transplant.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: So to have us exist to help and inspire people means that we are getting some incredible footballers.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "And that really is the power of it: to that transplant community or to the world, showing people that when you've had organ failure, your life isn't over.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: There is a chance for you, and you can go and resume and live your life." As the recipient of a donor heart, Jackson has to manage his exercise workload more carefully than his team-mates, many of whom have had kidney transplants, the most common transplant in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: His role in the side tends to involve 10-minute bursts, rather than playing for the duration of matches.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: He was sidelined for nearly five months, undergoing specialist cardiac monitoring, before returning to play.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "Of course it was extremely scary," he says, "but at that stage, when you are critically ill, there's not really much you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: You have to accept it." The super urgent waiting list he was placed on is the highest priority of the three tiers of patients waiting for a new heart.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Typically, only about four or five people are on the list at any one time in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Dr Paul Callan, a consultant cardiologist at Wythenshawe Hospital's Heart and Lung Centre, worked with Jackson during his diagnosis and recovery.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: "Initially, we used to quote an average wait of seven days on the urgent transplant list," he says.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: There are 8,700 people currently waiting for a donor organ, a figure that NHS Blood and Transplant say is an all-time high.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: This Organ Donation Week, , external which runs from 21-28 September, the NHS has launched an urgent response plan to address the decline.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: Jackson has yet to meet the family of the donor from which he received his new heart.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: He says he is considering reaching out to them around the two-year anniversary of his surgery.
sentences.article_title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner

sentences.text: For him to make a recovery within that time frame, culminating in playing football in a Transplant World Cup, is "remarkable", according to Dr Callan.

sentences.text: Hampshire Police were notified of the incident during the match and launched an investigation immediately afterwards, but this has been concluded.
sentences.article_title: FA charges Cardiff's Bielik as police end inquiry

sentences.text: "After speaking with the complainant and reviewing all available evidence, the matter has been resolved by way of an out-of-court disposal, agreed by all parties involved.

sentences.article_title: FA charges Cardiff's Bielik as police end inquiry

sentences.text: British journalist Mark Doyle, best known for his reporting on conflicts in Africa in the 1990s and 2000s, has died aged 67 after a short illness.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: After living in Africa, he joined the BBC in 1986.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: Doyle became East Africa correspondent in 1993 and made his mark covering the Rwandan genocide a year later.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: As West Africa correspondent from 1997 to 2002, he reported on Sierra Leone's brutal civil war and aftermath of Liberia's conflict.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: Following Doyle's death, BBC foreign editor Paul Danahar said he was a "legendary figure", as well as a "brilliant, brave, empathetic reporter".
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: The BBC's Andrew Harding, who worked with Doyle, paid tribute to his former colleague in a 2015 article, published to mark his departure from the national broadcaster.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: In the piece Fergal Keane, another prominent BBC correspondent in Africa, recalled their stint in Rwanda in 1994.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: "He stayed longer than any of us," Keane said of Doyle.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: "Those who were in that awful place at that awful time will know what Mark Doyle gave for the cause of truth and for the BBC." In the same article Sir David Richards, who headed British forces struggling to stop Sierra Leone's civil war in 2000, also praised Doyle.

sentences.text: Sir David said his reporting helped convince the UK government of the need for a robust intervention.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: "Hence the saving of thousands of Sierra Leonean lives that would otherwise have been at huge risk," he said.
sentences.article_title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67

sentences.text: Nigeria's men failed to qualify for both the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups As Nigeria begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign, former international Segun Odegbami, who won the tournament on home soil in 1980, says the country is experiencing the "worst time" in its football history.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Over the past 12 months both the Super Eagles and Super Falcons failed to qualify for their respective Fifa World Cups.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Odegbami says the diminishing returns represent a "tectonic shift" for one of the continent's traditional powers.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Our girls (the Super Falcons), who were African champions, failed to win a competition (the 2025 Women's Afcon) that was just there for their taking.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: All our junior teams are not doing well.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "Our local league is not bringing in money.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Something is definitely wrong." The crisis has already triggered major changes within the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Its president Ibrahim Gusau, general secretary Mohammed Sanusi and multiple members of the federation's executive committee resigned last month following mounting criticism.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "The outcry by Nigerians was total.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: Everybody wanted them out, to the extent that the President of the country himself (Bola Tinubu) made the pronouncement that he wanted reforms," he said.

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: "[We need to] develop national teams, harness talent from the grassroots and have governance that incorporates all forms of stakeholders.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.article_title: Nigerian football enduring 'worst time in history' - Odegbami

sentences.text: David Etor's first break came after designing and building a kind of "solar oven" in Nigeria A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith was the only South African to win a gold medal at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa’s most decorated Olympian But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult." Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete." While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I don't have to eat at a certain time, I don't have to sleep at a certain time, I don't have to think about travelling or not spending time with family anymore.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The world is so overwhelming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's like, in which direction to go?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was definitely the toughest season that I had to go through.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I think it's probably why it's made me a stronger person." Smith married her husband Joel in November 2023 and says family life was one of the reasons behind her decision to retire Initially, Smith took on speaking engagements to pay the bills.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: She smiles when she admits: "I hate public speaking.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I hate being in front of people." The same cannot be said of her love for competition.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Having returned to the pool in order to keep fit, she decided to have a crack at triathlon, something she describes as a "crazy idea".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The training was so intense, and I was like, 'OK, I might as well just go back to swimming if I'm going to train this hard'," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Every time I went back to the swimming pool and I dived in, I was like, 'Yeah, this is a feeling that I really miss so much'.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think slowly over the year and a half, I just realised 'Wow, I really do love swimming'." Having made her decision to come out of retirement, Smith now wants to freshen things up and "try something new".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: That means a change to the 50m breaststroke, an event which has just been added to the Olympic schedule for the first time ahead of the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I thought, 'Why don't I try?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Why don't I give myself that challenge?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Reinvent myself'," said Smith.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I always try and describe it to someone that maybe doesn't understand swimming; it's like a 400m runner and a 100m [runner].
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's two different body types, two different trainings, and that's where I'm going." It means she has more than halved her training volume, with three sessions a week instead of eight - a change she believes will help her retain her love for her sport and live a more balanced life.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I feel like I'm being so lazy because I used to do 12km per day and now the focus is on taking time to be as explosive as possible.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Now I'm doing 12km over a whole week.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I have 20 years of endurance in my pocket, but I can definitely see I don't have those fast twitch [muscle] fibres.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's a whole different way of teaching my body how to swim." Those initial 20 years in the pool left Smith feeling burned out.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Now she says she has earned the right to do things on her terms.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Swimming was an opportunity given to me by my parents and I believe I took it on full heartedly.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But, for the first time, it's my decision whether I want to come back.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I've achieved way more than I ever dreamed in my whole life, so I have nothing to prove." BBC African Sports Personality of the Year 2021: Tatjana Schoenmaker profile.

sentences.text: Real players wore T-shirts carrying the message 'Todos somos Caballas' - 'We are all Caballas' - before Tuesday's match against Elche.

sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: More than 100 people died when tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the territory from neighbouring Morocco in July.

sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I want to explain this clearly so people understand," the France international said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was the clubs' decision to include the T-shirt and to have us wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: We players had to wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "The first thing I want to say is that I stand in full solidarity with Ceuta and with all the victims.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "Because before I'm a player, I'm a human being.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "But I also wanted to make a gesture and spare a thought for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in harsh condition." Mbappe acknowledged his gesture could be misunderstood.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It wasn't an easy position to take," he said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was difficult because, in the end, people might think I'm against the people of Ceuta.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I have nothing against them, and I support them 100% in my thoughts.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: But I also wanted to spare a thought for all the people who are suffering because, at the end of the day, I'm human, and I don't want to prioritise one form of suffering over another.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "There are people who are suffering, and it breaks my heart to see that happening in the world.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: I'm a young man who wants the best for the world we live in.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row
